_comment: The curated MCP integration catalog the kernel ships (internal/integrations). Generated 2026-11-06 from configs/mcp.json.example and configs/mcp.integrations.json.example (policies, args, env) plus product metadata; see configs/MCP.md for the review notes behind each pin. Edit entries here directly from now on, and keep MCP.md in step. A deployment adds or replaces entries with mcp.catalog_file (same shape). Every entry declares its tool policy (tools and/or default_tool_policy) or says fail_closed: true; the loader refuses one that does neither.

entries.name: Brave Search
entries.description: Web, news, image and local search through the Brave Search API.

fields.name: BRAVE_API_KEY
fields.label: Brave Search API key
fields.help: From api-dashboard.search.brave.com. Paid beyond the free tier.

entries.notes: Official Brave Search server (brave/brave-search-mcp-server, MIT). BRAVE_API_KEY. Paid API beyond the free tier.

entries.name: Tavily search
entries.description: Search, extract, crawl and map the web through Tavily.

fields.name: TAVILY_API_KEY
fields.label: Tavily API key
fields.help: From app.tavily.com.

entries.notes: Official Tavily server (tavily-ai/tavily-mcp, MIT): search, extract, crawl, map. TAVILY_API_KEY. Paid API.

entries.name: Exa search
entries.description: Neural web search, code context and crawling through Exa.

fields.name: EXA_API_KEY
fields.label: Exa API key
fields.help: From dashboard.exa.ai.

entries.notes: Official Exa server (exa-labs/exa-mcp-server, MIT). EXA_API_KEY. Paid API.

entries.description: Keyless meta-search against your own SearXNG instance.

fields.name: SEARXNG_URL
fields.label: SearXNG URL
fields.help: Base URL of your SearXNG instance.

entries.name: Web search (DuckDuckGo, no key)
entries.description: Keyless web search through DuckDuckGo. Rate-limited; use a keyed provider for production.
entries.notes: Keyless DuckDuckGo search (nickclyde/duckduckgo-mcp-server, MIT, community). Rate-limited by DuckDuckGo; for production use a keyed provider (brave-search/tavily/exa) or self-hosted SearXNG from mcp.integrations.json.example.

entries.name: Web page fetch
entries.description: Fetch a URL and return it as Markdown.
entries.notes: Official reference server (modelcontextprotocol/servers, MIT). Fetches a URL and returns Markdown. Network read: egress, no approval. It can reach localhost/intranet URLs - see MCP.md trust notes.

entries.name: Google Workspace, one shared account (Gmail, Drive, Calendar)
entries.description: One Google account for every principal, read-only. For people, use google-workspace-personal.

fields.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
fields.label: OAuth client ID
fields.help: From your Google Cloud project (APIs & Services > Credentials, Desktop app).

fields.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
fields.label: OAuth client secret
fields.help: From the same OAuth client.

fields.name: USER_GOOGLE_EMAIL
fields.label: Google account email
fields.help: The account the agents act as.

entries.notes: Gmail, Drive, Calendar (taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp, MIT, community; Google's own remote Workspace MCP servers are preview and OAuth-only). GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET from your Cloud project; first use opens a browser OAuth consent and caches the user's token on disk (one Google account for every principal). --read-only drops send/modify tools; remove it AND the default_tool_policy to allow writes. SHARED ONLY: this stdio mode has no injected-token mode, so it cannot be per user; it acts as the single account whose consent is cached on the kernel host. Per-person Gmail/Drive/Calendar: google-workspace-personal (read) and google-workspace-personal-write (ADR-0141 owner position 5).

entries.name: Google Workspace, per person (Gmail, Drive, Calendar read)
entries.description: Each person's own Gmail, Drive and Calendar, read-only, with their own Google sign-in.
entries.notes: PER USER (ADR-0140/0141): every request carries the requesting person's own Google access token (Authorization: Bearer); the server holds no token and never refreshes (the premium accounts plugin refreshes). The kernel does NOT launch this server: the operator runs workspace-mcp 2.3.0 in external-OAuth mode as a loopback HTTP sidecar, outside the ADR-0139 D8 stdio sandbox (run it in a container where that matters): uvx workspace-mcp==2.3.0 --transport streamable-http --tools gmail drive calendar --tool-tier extended --read-only with MCP_ENABLE_OAUTH21=true EXTERNAL_OAUTH21_PROVIDER=true WORKSPACE_MCP_STATELESS_MODE=true WORKSPACE_MCP_HOST=127.0.0.1 GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=<the client id stored as oauth:google:client_id> PORT=8000. WORKSPACE_MCP_HOST=127.0.0.1 is required: with OAuth 2.1 on, the server binds 0.0.0.0 by default. It validates each token against Google userinfo (hence openid+email) and does not check the token's audience, so keep it on loopback. --read-only requests only read scopes and drops write tools; the dangerous tool list is defence in depth. Operator: a Google Cloud OAuth client (Web application) with redirect URI <CAMBRIAN_ACCOUNTS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/oauth/callback, Gmail/Calendar/Drive APIs enabled, stored as oauth:google:client_id / client_secret. gmail.readonly and drive.readonly are Google RESTRICTED scopes: an External-audience app needs Google verification (security assessment); an Internal (Workspace-only) app does not. Live handshake not verified (ticket T-20261106-per-user-google-workspace-curated-server-cannot). Google's own remote servers (gmailmcp/calendarmcp/drivemcp.googleapis.com) are Developer Preview: see configs/MCP.md.

entries.name: Google Workspace, per person (send mail, manage events)
entries.description: Each person's own Gmail and Calendar with send, draft and event tools; every write needs approval.
entries.notes: Same server as google-workspace-personal with Gmail send/draft and Calendar create/update/delete (manage_event covers all three). A separate entry so the read entry's grant never holds send scopes: each person signs in once per entry (grants are per server and person). Fail-closed: any tool not listed is dangerous. Operator-run loopback sidecar, NOT launched by the kernel: uvx workspace-mcp==2.3.0 --transport streamable-http --tools gmail calendar --tool-tier extended --disabled-tools manage_gmail_label manage_gmail_filter list_gmail_filters modify_gmail_message_labels create_calendar manage_out_of_office manage_focus_time with MCP_ENABLE_OAUTH21=true EXTERNAL_OAUTH21_PROVIDER=true WORKSPACE_MCP_STATELESS_MODE=true WORKSPACE_MCP_HOST=127.0.0.1 GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=<the client id stored as oauth:google:client_id> PORT=8001. Prompt injection: a mail the agent reads can ask it to send data out; send stays dangerous (approval) and should not be granted to profiles that read untrusted mail unattended. gmail.send/compose are Google sensitive scopes, gmail.readonly restricted (verification for External apps). Live handshake not verified.

entries.name: Microsoft 365 (Outlook, OneDrive, Calendar)
entries.description: Outlook mail, calendar, OneDrive, contacts and to-do through Microsoft Graph (read-only).

fields.name: MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID
fields.label: App (client) ID
fields.help: Shared mode only (one account for everyone, device-code sign-in on the kernel host). Per-user mode uses the OAuth client stored as oauth:microsoft:client_id.

fields.name: MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID
fields.label: Tenant ID
fields.help: Your Entra tenant; leave empty for the common endpoint.

entries.notes: Outlook mail, calendar, OneDrive, (with --org-mode) Teams and SharePoint via Microsoft Graph (Softeria/ms-365-mcp-server, MIT, community; Microsoft's own Agent 365 / Work IQ servers are tenant-managed and OAuth-only). Device-code sign-in on first use; token cached on disk. --read-only drops write tools; remove it AND the default_tool_policy to allow sending. PER USER (ADR-0140): each person connects their own Microsoft account from the console (Accounts in the console; premium accounts plugin, ADR-0141); the kernel runs one server process per person with that person's token in MS365_MCP_OAUTH_TOKEN (the server's bring-your-own-token mode; it does not refresh, so the kernel refreshes and relaunches). The operator registers an Entra app (delegated, read-only Graph scopes above) with redirect URI <CAMBRIAN_ACCOUNTS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/oauth/callback (premium accounts plugin, ADR-0141) and stores oauth:microsoft:client_id / client_secret. The client/tenant fields below are only for the shared (device-code) mode.

entries.name: Slack
entries.description: Read channels, threads and search; posting needs approval and is off unless enabled.

fields.name: SLACK_MCP_XOXP_TOKEN
fields.label: User token (xoxp-)
fields.help: A Slack user OAuth token. Set this OR the bot token.

fields.name: SLACK_MCP_XOXB_TOKEN
fields.label: Bot token (xoxb-)
fields.help: A bot token: invited channels only, no search.

fields.name: SLACK_MCP_ADD_MESSAGE_TOOL
fields.label: Enable posting
fields.help: Set to true (or a channel list) to expose the posting tool. Posting always needs approval.

entries.notes: Slack (korotovsky/slack-mcp-server, MIT, community; Slack's official remote server at mcp.slack.com is OAuth-only with no dynamic client registration). User token xoxp- in SLACK_MCP_XOXP_TOKEN (or bot xoxb- in SLACK_MCP_XOXB_TOKEN: invited channels only, no search). Posting is OFF unless SLACK_MCP_ADD_MESSAGE_TOOL is set; it is dangerous here either way. PER USER (ADR-0140): each person connects their own Slack account; their user token (xoxp-, read scopes only; posting would need chat:write, which is not requested) goes into SLACK_MCP_XOXP_TOKEN of a process run for that person alone. The shared token fields below are not given to per-user processes.

entries.name: Files (one folder)
entries.description: Read, search and (with approval) write files inside ONE folder you choose.

fields.name: FILESYSTEM_ROOT
fields.label: Folder to expose
fields.help: Absolute path of the only folder the server may reach, e.g. C:\Users\me\Documents\shared. Nothing outside it is reachable.

entries.notes: Official reference server. ONLY the directories given as args are reachable - replace ./workspace with the absolute roots you want to expose. Pinned to 1.0.0 because 2.x declares node>=24 (2.2.0 is current). Write tools are dangerous.

entries.name: Document reader (PDF / Office)
entries.description: Read PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX and HTML as Markdown; outline and search.
entries.notes: @sylphx/pdf-reader-mcp (now the SylphxAI/anymd project, MIT): PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/HTML to Markdown, outline, search, page render/OCR. A `source` may be a URL, so reads carry egress. Unlisted tools fail closed.

entries.name: MarkItDown (Office to Markdown)
entries.description: Convert Office, PDF, HTML, CSV and images to Markdown.
entries.notes: Microsoft MarkItDown MCP (microsoft/markitdown, MIT; package is pre-release 0.0.1a8): converts docx/xlsx/pptx/pdf/html/csv/images to Markdown. The uri may be http(s), file: or data:, so reads carry egress. Upstream says local, trusted use only. Needs --prerelease=allow: a transitive dependency (azure-ai-contentunderstanding) is only published as a pre-release. Handshake verified 2026-11-05 (tool: convert_to_markdown).

entries.name: Excel workbooks
entries.description: Create and edit .xlsx workbooks. Every tool needs approval.

fields.name: EXCEL_FILES_PATH
fields.label: Working folder
fields.help: Folder the server reads and writes workbooks in.

entries.notes: Optional, keyless: create/edit .xlsx (haris-musa/excel-mcp-server, MIT, community). EXCEL_FILES_PATH (not a secret) is its working directory. Fails closed.

entries.name: Word documents
entries.description: Create and edit .docx documents. Every tool needs approval.
entries.notes: Optional, keyless: create/edit .docx (GongRzhe/Office-Word-MCP-Server, MIT, community; last release 2025-12-31). Fails closed. Reading Office files is better served by markitdown/pdf-reader in mcp.json.example.

entries.name: PostgreSQL database
entries.description: Inspect and query a PostgreSQL database. Raw SQL needs approval; connect with a read-only role.

fields.name: POSTGRES_HOST
fields.label: Host
fields.help: Database host name.

fields.name: POSTGRES_PORT
fields.label: Port
fields.help: Database port.

fields.name: POSTGRES_DATABASE
fields.label: Database
fields.help: Database name.

fields.name: POSTGRES_USER
fields.label: User
fields.help: Prefer a read-only role.

fields.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
fields.label: Password
fields.help: The role's password.

fields.name: POSTGRES_QUERY_PARAMS
fields.label: Connection parameters
fields.help: Optional, e.g. sslmode=require.

entries.notes: Google MCP Toolbox, prebuilt postgres toolset (Apache-2.0). The reference @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres is deprecated. Connect with a READ-ONLY database role: execute_sql takes raw SQL. get_query_plan is kept dangerous because it templates caller SQL.

entries.name: SQLite database
entries.description: Query a SQLite file. Raw SQL needs approval; use a copy of the file.

fields.name: SQLITE_DATABASE
fields.label: Database file
fields.help: Path to the .db / .sqlite file.

entries.notes: Google MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/mcp-toolbox, Apache-2.0), prebuilt sqlite toolset. The reference mcp-server-sqlite is archived. SQLITE_DATABASE (kernel env) names the database file. execute_sql takes raw SQL and can write: dangerous. Point it at a copy or open a read-only file when you only need analysis.

entries.name: GitHub (read-only)
entries.description: Repositories, issues, pull requests and Actions, read-only.

fields.name: GITHUB_MCP_PAT
fields.label: GitHub personal access token
fields.help: Shared mode only. Per-user mode: each person connects their own GitHub account from the console.

entries.notes: Official GitHub MCP server, remote (github/github-mcp-server, MIT). /readonly keeps only read tools. Fine-grained PAT in GITHUB_MCP_PAT (repo read scopes). For writes use the github-write entry below. PER USER (ADR-0140): each person connects their own GitHub account; every request carries that person's token (Authorization: Bearer). Register a GitHub App (its user-to-server tokens carry the app's fine-grained permissions, so no OAuth scopes are requested; give it read-only repository permissions for this entry) with callback <CAMBRIAN_ACCOUNTS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/oauth/callback (premium accounts plugin, ADR-0141), and store oauth:github:client_id / client_secret.

entries.name: GitHub (read and write)
entries.description: GitHub with create/update tools. Every tool needs approval until you list the read tools.

fields.name: GITHUB_MCP_PAT
fields.label: GitHub personal access token
fields.help: Shared mode only. Per-user mode: each person connects their own GitHub account from the console.

entries.notes: Same server with write tools (issues, PRs, files, branches). No default policy: every tool is dangerous (approval) until you list read tools explicitly. Use a PAT scoped to the repos the agents may change. PER USER (ADR-0140): each person connects their own GitHub account; every request carries that person's token (Authorization: Bearer). Register a GitHub App (its user-to-server tokens carry the app's fine-grained permissions, so no OAuth scopes are requested; give it read-only repository permissions for this entry) with callback <CAMBRIAN_ACCOUNTS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/oauth/callback (premium accounts plugin, ADR-0141), and store oauth:github:client_id / client_secret.

entries.name: Git (one repository)
entries.description: History, diffs and (with approval) commits and branches in ONE repository. No push.

fields.name: GIT_REPOSITORY
fields.label: Repository path
fields.help: Absolute path of the git repository.

entries.notes: Official reference server. --repository scopes it to one repo; replace the path. History and diff reads are safe; anything that changes the index, HEAD or branches is dangerous. It has no push tool.

entries.name: Notion
entries.description: Search and read Notion pages and databases. Every tool needs approval until you list the read ones.

fields.name: NOTION_TOKEN
fields.label: Integration secret
fields.help: An internal integration secret (notion.so/my-integrations), shared only with the pages it may touch.

entries.notes: Official Notion server, local (makenotion/notion-mcp-server, MIT). NOTION_TOKEN = an internal integration secret shared only with the pages it may touch. Notion now prioritises its remote server (mcp.notion.com, OAuth-only). Tool names are generated from Notion's OpenAPI spec, so none are listed: every tool is dangerous until you list the read ones.

entries.name: Atlassian (Jira, Confluence)
entries.description: Jira, Confluence, JSM, Bitbucket and Compass through Atlassian's hosted server. Writes need approval.

fields.name: ATLASSIAN_MCP_API_KEY
fields.label: Service account API key
fields.help: Needs an org admin to enable API-token auth for the Rovo MCP server.

entries.notes: Official Atlassian Rovo MCP server, remote (Jira, Confluence, JSM, Bitbucket, Compass). Headless auth needs an org admin to enable API-token auth; a service-account API key goes in ATLASSIAN_MCP_API_KEY (Bearer). A personal token instead needs Authorization: Basic base64(email:token): use auth {type: header, header: Authorization, token_env: ...} with the full 'Basic ...' value. Writes exist: no default policy.

entries.name: Linear (read-only)
entries.description: Find issues, projects and comments in Linear (read-only).

fields.name: LINEAR_API_KEY
fields.label: Linear API key
fields.help: Linear > Settings > Security & access > Personal API keys.

entries.notes: Official Linear MCP server, remote. Accepts a Linear API key as Bearer. /mcp/readonly exposes read tools only; use https://mcp.linear.app/mcp (and drop the default policy) for writes.

entries.name: Code sandbox (Docker)
entries.description: Run Python (and JS, R, Go) for data analysis in a throwaway Docker container; plots come back as images.

fields.name: BACKEND
fields.label: Container backend
fields.help: docker (default), podman or kubernetes.

fields.name: SANDBOX_NETWORK_MODE
fields.label: Network
fields.help: none keeps the sandbox offline (on-demand pip installs then fail: use an image with your libraries).

fields.name: SANDBOX_READ_ONLY
fields.label: Read-only root filesystem
fields.help: true hardens the container.

fields.name: SANDBOX_CAP_DROP
fields.label: Dropped capabilities
fields.help: ALL drops every Linux capability.

fields.name: SANDBOX_SECURITY_OPT
fields.label: Security options
fields.help: no-new-privileges:true blocks privilege escalation.

fields.name: SANDBOX_MEMORY
fields.label: Memory limit
fields.help: e.g. 2g.

fields.name: SANDBOX_CPU_COUNT
fields.label: CPU limit
fields.help: Number of CPUs.

fields.name: DOCKER_HOST
fields.label: Docker host
fields.help: Only if Docker is not on the default socket.

entries.notes: Sandboxed code execution for data analysis (vndee/llm-sandbox, MIT). Runs Python (and JS, R, Go, ...) in a throwaway Docker container; captures matplotlib plots as images; installs pandas/numpy on demand. Needs Docker running. HARDEN via the kernel environment: BACKEND=docker SANDBOX_NETWORK_MODE=none SANDBOX_READ_ONLY=true SANDBOX_CAP_DROP=ALL SANDBOX_SECURITY_OPT=no-new-privileges:true SANDBOX_MEMORY=2g SANDBOX_CPU_COUNT=1 (with network none, on-demand pip installs fail: pre-bake an image). execute_code is dangerous with write+egress until those settings are proven to take.

entries.name: Terminal (Desktop Commander)
entries.description: PowerShell / cmd / bash sessions, file operations and process management. Every write or exec needs approval. Not a sandbox.
entries.notes: Desktop Commander (@wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander, MIT): Windows/macOS/Linux terminal (PowerShell/cmd/bash sessions, REPLs), file ops, search, process management. Handshake verified on Windows 2026-11-05 (25 tools). NOT a sandbox: its allowedDirectories restricts only its file tools, never terminal commands, and its blockedCommands list is bypassable (upstream README). Every write/exec tool is dangerous (approval required). NEVER grant set_config_value to an agent (it can widen its own allowedDirectories/blockedCommands) nor give_feedback_to_desktop_commander. Telemetry is ON by default upstream: set "telemetryEnabled": false in ~/.claude-server-commander/config.json (done on the owner's host 2026-11-05). For isolation run its Docker image (ADR-0139 D8).

entries.name: Shell (allow-listed commands)
entries.description: Run only the executables you allow. Not a sandbox: allowed programs run with the kernel user's rights. Linux and macOS only.

fields.name: ALLOW_COMMANDS
fields.label: Allowed commands
fields.help: Comma-separated executables, e.g. git,ls,cat. Never an interpreter, curl or a package manager.

fields.name: ALLOW_PATTERNS
fields.label: Allowed patterns
fields.help: Optional regex patterns of allowed commands.

entries.notes: Replacement for the dead @cfdude/super-shell-mcp (npm 404). tumf/mcp-shell-server (MIT): runs ONLY executables named in ALLOW_COMMANDS (set it in the kernel environment, e.g. ALLOW_COMMANDS=git,ls,cat). It is NOT a sandbox: an allowed program runs with the kernel user's files, network and credentials. Always dangerous. Windows execution is unverified (developed for POSIX shells). VERIFIED 2026-11-05: does NOT run on Windows (imports the Unix-only `pwd` module); use it only on Linux/macOS deployments.

entries.name: Browser (Playwright)
entries.description: Drive a real headless browser: navigate, click, fill forms. Every tool needs approval.
entries.notes: Optional, keyless: Microsoft Playwright browser automation (microsoft/playwright-mcp, Apache-2.0). Drives a real browser: navigates, clicks, fills forms, can submit anything. --isolated keeps no profile between sessions. Every tool fails closed (dangerous). First run downloads a browser build.

entries.name: Time and time zones
entries.description: Current time and time-zone conversion.
entries.notes: Official reference server: current time and timezone conversion. Pure read.

entries.name: Calculator
entries.description: Exact arithmetic, so the model does not multiply in its head.
entries.notes: Exact arithmetic (githejie/mcp-server-calculator, MIT, community, ~160 stars). One tool, calculate(expression): an AST walker over numbers, + - * / // % ** and the math module (pi, e, sqrt, log, ...); no eval, no I/O, no network. Pure read. Caveat: a huge power (9**9**9) is not capped and can spin the server until call_timeout_ms. PyPI 0.2.1 (2026-08-08) checked on the registry 2026-11-05; live handshake NOT verified yet.

entries.name: Sequential thinking
entries.description: A scratchpad for step-by-step reasoning. No I/O.
entries.notes: Official reference server: a scratchpad for step-by-step reasoning. No I/O. Pinned to 1.0.0 because 2.x declares node>=24.
